facts.statement: Athabascasaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur belonging to the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
facts.quote: Athabascasaurus is an extinct genus of platypterygiine ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known from Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected in 2000 from an open-pit mine near Fort McMurray, Alberta.
facts.quote: It was collected in 2000 on the western side of the Syncrude Canada Ltd.'s Base Mine, an open-pit mine near Fort McMurray.

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Patrick S. Druckenmiller and Erin E. Maxwell in 2010.
facts.quote: Athabascasaurus was first named by Patrick S. Druckenmiller and Erin E. Maxwell in 2010

facts.statement: Athabascasaurus lived during the earliest Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in the Wabiskaw Member of the Clearwater Formation, which dates to the earliest Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous epoch, about 112 million years ago.

facts.statement: Athabascasaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur reaching a length of 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: Athabascasaurus is a medium-sized ichthyosaur, measuring 3.5 m long.

facts.statement: A unique feature of the genus is that each postfrontal bone bears a triangular projection extending over the adjacent postorbital bone.
facts.quote: Each postfrontal (a paired skull roof bone) of Athabascasaurus bears a triangular projection that extends on top of the upper part of the adjacent postorbital (paired bones located behind the orbits), a unique feature of the genus.

facts.statement: Athabascasaurus had only 42 vertebrae in front of the hips, an unusually low number for ophthalmosaurs, measuring 1.509 meters in the holotype.
facts.quote: There are 42 vertebrae in front of the hips Athtabascasaurus, an unusually low number for ophthalmosaurs, with this series measuring 1.509 m long in the holotype.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses suggest Athabascasaurus is most closely related to Platypterygius australis and nests within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
facts.quote: Two cladistic analyses by Fischer and colleagues, one in 2011 and the other in 2012, found it to be most closely related to "Platypterygius" australis, and to nest within Platypterygiinae.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses found Athabascasaurus closely related to Platypterygius australis, leading to its inclusion in the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
facts.quote: Análisis cladísticos recientes encontraron que estaba cercanamente relacionado con "Platypterygius" australis, y fue por tanto incluido en la subfamilia Platypterygiinae.

facts.statement: The time range for Athabascasaurus is estimated from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

rejected.statement: In Athabascasaurus, the ischium and pubis are fused into a single unit called an ischiopubis.
rejected.quote: The two lower hip bones, the ischium and pubis, are fused into a single unit known as an ischiopubis.
